**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The document contains no most-favoured-nation obligation burdening Northwind. The only parity provision runs in our favour:

- **§ 7.6 (p0031)** — Brightline warrants that Fees charged to us will be no less favourable than fees offered to any similarly situated customer for comparable volumes and terms. This is a Vendor-granted MFN, exactly what the playbook welcomes, and per the direction rule it must not be flagged.

I also checked the sections where a Customer-side parity or best-terms clause would typically sit:
- **§ 4 (Order Forms and Affiliate Orders)** — change-order mechanics only; no pricing-parity or offer-matching obligation.
- **§ 30 (General)** — standard boilerplate; no MFN, exclusivity, or preferred-supplier undertaking.
- Full-text searches for "most favoured nation", "no less favourable", "best terms", and price/offer-matching language returned nothing beyond § 7.6.

This sits at the **preferred** position (no MFN obligation on Customer), not merely the fallback, so no 12-month/defined-product limitation analysis is needed. Recommend leaving § 7.6 as drafted — deleting or softening it would forfeit a benefit to us.
